checks.summary: V2-075 disclosed that three of its twelve invocations were consumed by provider-side transient failures: the first attempt at I1 (ledger sequence 1) and the two entries of the first attempt at the I5/I6 phase (sequences 6 and 7), one more such phase than V2-063 saw. This gate re-read the ledger file on disk and confirmed the disclosure against the physical record: all twelve entries are present, sequence 1 settled with no session id, sequences 6 and 9 are the reserved never-settled sigkill entries, sequence 7 settled with no session id, and no entry was erased or rewritten. Ruling under G5: these are not flaky results overwritten by retry. In each failed attempt the CLI returned a parsed non-success with zero usage counts and no session id, the same shape the deliberately unreachable I7 probe produces, so the behaviour under verification was never observed to vary; the probe failed to take place, the re-run changed not one byte of source, both attempts stand disclosed in the record and in the ledger, and every one of the nine PASS verdicts comes from an attempt that succeeded. The exhaustion itself (invocation_count 12 of max 12, halted false, settled 0.4441 USD of 8.00) is a fact about future headroom, not a defect in this evidence: Reserve's guard admitted the twelfth reservation lawfully, thresholds were never raised, and the runbook now instructs the next operator to obtain a new approved record. The rising transient rate (one phase in V2-063, two in V2-075) is noted for the coordinator as an observation, not a gate condition.

checks.name: g6a-classification-and-re-execution-at-the-judgment-commit
argv: devbox run --pure -- make check; devbox run --pure -- make component-docs; devbox run --pure -- make component-infra; devbox run --pure -- make component-tooling
checks.summary: Classification of every ground by what re-executes its checks, as instruction and rule G6a require. G6a (re-executed by make check at the judgment commit): ev-v2-016-runner (go test over runner, provider, contracts, race runs, all inside the test target), ev-v2-047-provider-preflight-contract, ev-v2-048-execution-identifier and ev-v2-050-runaway-guard (contracts, release and docs-guard tests, gofmt via the format target), and 20 of the 23 ev-v2-018 component re-issues, whose component targets are go test invocations strictly contained in make check's test target, plus store-firestore which make check runs explicitly under the emulator. Their freshness basis is the measured green: make check at judgment commit 56fbc4ac01842eb347bffb378f883189d6b799bf on a clean tree exited 0 with verdicts 'ok' for all 17 tested packages and no FAIL line, gitleaks '460 commits scanned' then 'no leaks found', and 'workflow-pins: 3 unique (owner/repo, version) -> sha pins, no disagreement'. Three component targets are not inside make check, so this gate re-executed each directly at the judgment commit rather than trusting any stored record: make component-docs exited 0 silently (its check is a negative rg scan), make component-infra printed 'Success! The configuration is valid.' from tofu validate after the policy script, and make component-tooling is the vacuous @true, recorded as vacuous by design rather than as a verification. These re-runs add no evidence entry, per the witness re-run provision of G6. The previous judgment's 23 ev-v2-018 component re-issues are NOT reused as freshness claims: under the revised G6a per-component key equality is no longer a pass condition, because the claims those records carry are re-proven at this commit by the runs just described; the records remain G2 grounds of record integrity only. No re-issue of the 23 components is performed, because a re-issue would add provenance, not freshness, and the rule places freshness in the re-execution this gate paid for itself. Checks inside ground records that captured one-off historical facts (diff scopes, directory listings) are records of past observations, not re-executable freshness claims, and are not counted as such.

checks.summary: G6b requirement one: ev-v2-075 records observation commit d9f98ae573e617aafd82d87fa1c35f9bd6e26ffb and the published set artifact repeats it as observed_commit. The commit object exists in the repository and was inspected: it contains exactly the new preflight record and the two-constant repoint of internal/runner/provider_live_test.go, matching the record's account, and it predates every file this gate's diff measurement sees. One fact found by this gate and weighed rather than hidden: that commit, and the two later commits the record names, are reachable from no ref, because V2-075's branch was rebuilt with git update-ref and landed on main as a squashed commit. Section 9.1 explicitly accepts that rewrite, and this gate's own measurements confirm no content was lost: the tree diff from the observation commit to the judgment commit names no exercised file, and the runner component key at the judgment commit is byte-identical to the key measured at the observation commit, so the exercised bytes on the judged branch are exactly the observed bytes. The residual risk is durability, not integrity: an unreachable object can be pruned by a future gc, after which the G6b diff would become unmeasurable and re-observation would be forced. That is recorded as a remediation proposal, not as a defect of this evidence, because the measurement was performed now, against the existing object, and is transcribed below.

checks.name: gate-verdict
checks.summary: Verdict: the M3 gate passes at judgment commit 56fbc4ac01842eb347bffb378f883189d6b799bf. G1 through G5 and G7 are satisfied as measured above; G6a is satisfied by make check green at the judgment commit plus direct re-execution of the three component targets make check does not contain; G6b is satisfied for the single live ground ev-v2-075-provider-live-claude-rebind by the recorded observation commit and this gate's own empty-intersection measurement against the recomputed published set, with two positive controls proving the measurement non-vacuous. The revision of G6 was applied as a replacement, not a relaxation: the intersection was measured, not argued. Two disclosures from V2-075 were weighed and accepted: the three transient-failure invocations are preserved in the ledger and are not flaky overwrites, and the git update-ref rewrite lost no content, as proven by the tree diff and the key identity, leaving only an object-durability risk recorded as remediation. Remediation proposals for the coordinator, neither blocking this gate: first, anchor live observation commits under a durable ref (for example a local keep ref or tag created at observation time and named by the evidence record) so the G6b diff stays measurable against future gc, and anchor d9f98ae573e617aafd82d87fa1c35f9bd6e26ffb retroactively; second, track the provider-side transient failure rate across live exercises (one phase in V2-063, two in V2-075, identical zero-usage shape) and decide whether the suite should distinguish that shape from I7's induced transport failure in the ledger's purpose strings before the M6 multi-provider live work relies on the same machinery. This gate started no Provider CLI and made zero live invocations.
